q: A company is using Amazon ECR and wants to replicate container images to another AWS account for disaster recovery. Where must the registry permissions policy be configured?

opts.c: On both source and destination accounts

exp.a: Incorrect. The source account does not require any special repository or registry policies for cross-account replication.
exp.b: Correct. Cross-account ECR replication requires policy configuration on the destination account only. The source account does not require any special repository or registry policies. [4]
exp.c: Incorrect. Only the destination account needs the permissions policy.

exp.b: Incorrect. 15 is below the actual limit.

exp.d: Incorrect. 50 exceeds the actual limit.

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is much higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. 25 is the destination limit, not filter limit.

q: When was AWS App Mesh officially discontinued?

exp.a: Incorrect. September 24, 2024 was when new customer onboarding was blocked.
exp.b: Incorrect. December 2025 is not the discontinuation date.
exp.c: Correct. AWS App Mesh was discontinued effective September 30th, 2026. [5]
exp.d: Incorrect. March 2027 is not the correct date.

q: What is the recommended replacement for AWS App Mesh?

opts.b: Amazon ECS Service Connect

exp.a: Incorrect. Cloud Map is for service discovery, not a full service mesh replacement.

exp.c: Incorrect. Transit Gateway is for VPC connectivity.
exp.d: Incorrect. While VPC Lattice offers service-to-service connectivity, Service Connect is the direct migration path for App Mesh on ECS.

q: A team is comparing App Mesh to ECS Service Connect for observability. What is the key difference?

opts.a: App Mesh provides better CloudWatch integration
opts.b: Service Connect provides free application-level traffic metrics sent to CloudWatch automatically, while App Mesh requires you to capture and ship metrics yourself

exp.a: Incorrect. App Mesh requires manual metric configuration.
exp.b: Correct. With App Mesh, it's your responsibility to capture traffic metrics and ship them to a monitoring service. Service Connect provides free application-level traffic metrics sent to CloudWatch, visible in both the CloudWatch console and Amazon ECS console. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. Service Connect does provide built-in metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. Their observability capabilities differ significantly.

q: A team needs mutual TLS (mTLS) between their ECS services. Which service supports this?

opts.b: Only AWS App Mesh
opts.c: Both App Mesh and Service Connect

exp.a: Incorrect. Service Connect does not yet support mTLS.
exp.b: Correct. App Mesh has the ability to implement two-way peer authentication using mutual TLS (mTLS), a feature not yet available for Service Connect. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. mTLS is only available in App Mesh.
exp.d: Incorrect. App Mesh supports mTLS.

q: A company is migrating from App Mesh to Service Connect. They currently fine-tune outlier detection and retry parameters. What limitation will they face with Service Connect?

opts.a: Service Connect doesn't support any reliability features
opts.b: Service Connect has opinionated defaults with only timeouts being configurable, unlike App Mesh where all variables can be fine-tuned
opts.c: Service Connect requires more configuration than App Mesh
opts.d: There is no difference in configuration flexibility

exp.a: Incorrect. Service Connect does support reliability features.
exp.b: Correct. With App Mesh these variables can be fine-tuned, whereas with Service Connect there are opinionated defaults with only timeouts being configurable. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. Service Connect requires less configuration, not more.
exp.d: Incorrect. App Mesh provides more configuration flexibility.

q: A company wants to use TLS between their ECS services with Service Connect. What certificate type can they use that reduces cost compared to App Mesh?

opts.b: AWS PCA short-lived certificates instead of general purpose certificates

exp.a: Incorrect. Self-signed certificates aren't the recommended approach.
exp.b: Correct. Service Connect simplifies TLS configuration and you can use lower-cost AWS PCA short-lived certificates, compared to App Mesh which requires general purpose certificates from AWS Private Certificate Authority. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. ACM public certificates are for public endpoints.
exp.d: Incorrect. Let's Encrypt is not an AWS-native solution for this.

q: A company using ECS capacity providers launches a large number of tasks simultaneously across multiple services. The capacity provider is launching new EC2 instances, but task placement is slow. What is happening?

opts.b: The ECS service scheduler implements back-off and exponential throttling for task placement while waiting for new instances
opts.c: The tasks are too large for the instances
opts.d: The VPC has run out of IP addresses

exp.a: Incorrect. The ECS agent isn't crashing.
exp.b: Correct. When there is insufficient cluster capacity, the Amazon ECS service scheduler implements a back-off and exponential throttling strategy for retrying task placement as new container instances are launched, resulting in slower deployment times. [11]
exp.c: Incorrect. Task size isn't the primary issue here.
exp.d: Incorrect. IP exhaustion would cause different errors.

q: How can a team avoid slow deployments caused by ECS capacity provider throttling when launching many services simultaneously?

opts.b: Either deploy a limited number of services at a time or pre-scale the Auto Scaling group before deployment

exp.a: Incorrect. Task definition size doesn't solve the capacity issue.
exp.b: Correct. To avoid this situation, you can plan service deployments by either deploying a limited number at a time or pre-scaling infrastructure. [11]
exp.c: Incorrect. Disabling capacity providers removes auto-scaling capability.
exp.d: Incorrect. While Fargate avoids EC2 capacity issues, it may not suit all workloads.

q: What does Amazon ECS recommend for safely terminating EC2 instances that are running tasks?

opts.b: Use managed instance draining, which is enabled by default
opts.d: Remove instances from the cluster first

exp.a: Incorrect. Force stopping disrupts workloads.
exp.b: Correct. AWS recommends using managed instance draining to allow for graceful termination of Amazon EC2 instances. This feature is on by default. [13]
exp.c: Incorrect. Manual draining is unnecessary when managed draining is available.
exp.d: Incorrect. Removing from cluster before draining tasks can cause disruption.

q: A team wants to use both On-Demand and Spot Instances for their ECS service. How should they configure capacity providers?

opts.a: Use a single Auto Scaling group with mixed instances
opts.b: Create two capacity providers: one connected to an On-Demand Auto Scaling group and one to a Spot Auto Scaling group, then use a custom capacity provider strategy

exp.a: Incorrect. A single ASG with mixed instances doesn't provide the same control as separate capacity providers.
exp.b: Correct. Use two capacity providers connected to two Auto Scaling groups—one with 100% On-Demand and one with 100% Spot. A custom strategy configures a base of On-Demand tasks with remaining tasks split between providers. [7]
exp.c: Incorrect. While Fargate Spot exists, the question asks about EC2-based capacity.
exp.d: Incorrect. Manual management defeats the purpose of capacity providers.

q: A company configures a capacity provider strategy with a base of 2 tasks on On-Demand and equal weight for remaining tasks between On-Demand and Spot. If they scale to 12 tasks, how many run on each?

opts.b: 2 On-Demand (base) + 5 On-Demand + 5 Spot

exp.a: Incorrect. The base parameter gives On-Demand priority for the first 2 tasks.
exp.b: Correct logic structure but format differs.
exp.c: Correct. Base parameter places 2 tasks on On-Demand first. Remaining 10 tasks split equally: 5 On-Demand + 5 Spot. Total: 7 On-Demand, 5 Spot. [7]
exp.d: Incorrect. Equal weight means remaining tasks are split, not all going to Spot.

q: What does Amazon ECS recommend for instance type selection when using Spot Instances with capacity providers?

opts.a: Use a single large instance type
opts.b: Use attribute-based instance type selection for flexibility across multiple instance types
opts.c: Always use the cheapest instance type

exp.a: Incorrect. Single instance types reduce Spot availability.
exp.b: Correct. Use attribute-based instance type selection to select all instance types that match requirements (e.g., 2–4 vCPU, 4–8 GiB memory). Instance type flexibility is a key best practice for Spot Instances. [7]
exp.c: Incorrect. Cheapest isn't always best for availability.
exp.d: Incorrect. Graviton is good but flexibility is the priority.

q: What is the trade-off of instance type flexibility when using ECS Cluster Auto Scaling (CAS) with Spot?

opts.b: Scaling with CAS is fastest when using the same instance sizes, but flexibility is needed for Spot availability
opts.c: CAS doesn't work with Spot Instances

exp.a: Incorrect. There is a trade-off to consider.
exp.b: Correct. Scaling with Amazon ECS Cluster Auto Scaling (CAS) is fastest when using the same instance sizes; however, instance type flexibility is a key best practice for using Spot Instances. [7]
exp.c: Incorrect. CAS works with Spot Instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. Flexible instances don't necessarily cost more.

q: How does ECS managed scaling work with capacity providers?

opts.b: It creates an AWS Auto Scaling plan with a target tracking scaling policy associated with the Auto Scaling group
opts.d: It requires manual configuration of CloudWatch alarms

exp.a: Incorrect. Cron scheduling is not how managed scaling works.
exp.b: Correct. When you enable managed scaling, Amazon ECS creates an AWS Auto Scaling plan with a target tracking scaling policy and associates it with the Auto Scaling group. [7]
exp.c: Incorrect. Target tracking is used, not step scaling.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch alarms are created automatically, not manually.

q: A company is comparing Fargate vs EC2 for their EKS workloads. They need to pack multiple pods onto compute efficiently. Which option is better for cost?

opts.b: Free application-level traffic metrics sent to CloudWatch without additional configuration

exp.a: Incorrect. Grafana integration isn't the primary advantage.
exp.b: Correct. Service Connect provides free application-level networking metrics sent to CloudWatch, visible in both CloudWatch and Amazon ECS console, without requiring you to configure metric collection. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. Custom meshes may offer more customization but require more effort.
exp.d: Incorrect. While OTel support exists, the free CloudWatch metrics are the key advantage.

q: What happened to new AWS App Mesh customer onboarding starting September 24, 2024?

opts.b: New customers were blocked from onboarding to AWS App Mesh
opts.d: Only EKS customers could use App Mesh

exp.a: Incorrect. Significant changes occurred.
exp.b: Correct. Starting from September 24th, 2024, new customers were blocked from onboarding to AWS App Mesh. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. Pricing change was not the restriction.
exp.d: Incorrect. The restriction was a complete block on new customers.

q: An existing AWS App Mesh customer wants to know if they can still create new resources before the discontinuation date. What can they do?

opts.a: No new resources can be created
opts.b: Existing customers can use the service as normal, including creating new resources via CLI and CloudFormation until September 30, 2026

exp.a: Incorrect. Existing customers retain full capabilities.
exp.b: Correct. Until September 30, 2026, existing AWS App Mesh customers can use the service as normal, including creating new resources and onboarding new accounts via the AWS CLI and AWS CloudFormation. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. CLI and CloudFormation are both supported.
exp.d: Incorrect. Full read/write operations are permitted.

q: What proxy technology do both App Mesh and ECS Service Connect use?

opts.b: Envoy

exp.a: Incorrect. NGINX is not used by either service.
exp.b: Correct. Both App Mesh and Service Connect use Envoy's outlier detection, health checking, and retry mechanisms. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. HAProxy is not the underlying proxy.
exp.d: Incorrect. Traefik is not used.

q: A company using ECR replication wants to replicate images from us-west-2 (source) to both eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 within the same account. What must they do?

opts.a: Create separate replication configurations in each destination region
opts.b: Configure the replication rule in us-west-2 specifying their own account ID with both destination regions
opts.c: Contact AWS Support to enable multi-region replication

exp.a: Incorrect. Configuration is done in the source region.
exp.b: Correct. Create the replication rule in the source region (us-west-2) specifying your own account ID with multiple destination regions in a single rule. [1][6]
exp.c: Incorrect. Multi-region replication is self-service.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 CRR doesn't apply to ECR.

q: How does ECS Cluster Auto Scaling (CAS) differ from standard EC2 Auto Scaling?

opts.b: CAS creates an AWS Auto Scaling plan with a target tracking policy specifically designed for ECS task placement demand

exp.a: Incorrect. CAS is purpose-built for ECS.
exp.b: Correct. When managed scaling is enabled, Amazon ECS creates an AWS Auto Scaling plan with a target tracking scaling policy and associates it with the Auto Scaling group, specifically designed to match capacity to ECS task demand. [7]
exp.c: Incorrect. CAS uses target tracking, not just scheduled scaling.
exp.d: Incorrect. CAS is for EC2 capacity providers, not Fargate.

q: A Solutions Architect needs to recommend an approach for a team migrating from App Mesh to Service Connect. What should they consider regarding traffic routing flexibility?

opts.a: Service Connect offers more routing flexibility
opts.b: App Mesh provides more fine-grained traffic routing control, while Service Connect uses opinionated defaults; the team should evaluate if the simplified approach meets their needs

exp.a: Incorrect. App Mesh actually offers more routing flexibility.
exp.b: Correct. The migration post discusses the key differences in traffic routing, observability, security, and resource sharing, noting that Service Connect provides streamlined abstractions with opinionated defaults while App Mesh allows fine-tuning. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. Their routing capabilities differ.
exp.d: Incorrect. Both support traffic routing.

q: A company deploys 50 ECS services simultaneously, each with 100 tasks, using a capacity provider. What problem are they likely to encounter?

opts.b: Task placement will be throttled due to insufficient cluster capacity, with back-off and exponential retry as new instances launch
opts.d: The ECS cluster will be deleted

exp.a: Incorrect. Services will be created but task placement will be slow.
exp.b: Correct. When launching large numbers of tasks simultaneously, you can meet the quota for tasks in PROVISIONING state. The ECS service scheduler implements back-off and exponential throttling for retrying task placement as new instances launch. [11]
exp.c: Incorrect. There isn't enough capacity for immediate placement.
exp.d: Incorrect. The cluster won't be deleted.
